sets.title: Cell organization
sets.unlock_rule: Schedule only after every associated knowledge record has been encountered in a completed or in-progress story.

questions.prompt: A cell has DNA in a nucleoid region and lacks a membrane-bound nucleus.
questions.explanation: A prokaryotic cell lacks a membrane-bound nucleus.

questions.prompt: A cell encloses its DNA in a nucleus and contains membrane-bound organelles.
questions.explanation: A eukaryotic cell contains a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.

sets.title: Ribosome location and destination
sets.unlock_rule: Schedule only after every associated knowledge record has been encountered in a completed or in-progress story.

questions.prompt: These ribosomes generally make proteins that function in the cytosol.
questions.explanation: Free ribosomes are suspended in the cytosol and commonly make proteins used there.

questions.prompt: These ribosomes are attached to rough ER or the nuclear envelope and commonly make proteins for secretion or membranes.
questions.explanation: Bound ribosomes direct newly made proteins into the endomembrane pathway.

sets.title: ER identity
sets.unlock_rule: Schedule only after every associated knowledge record has been encountered in a completed or in-progress story.

questions.prompt: This membrane network has ribosomes attached and handles proteins entering the endomembrane pathway.
questions.explanation: Rough ER has bound ribosomes and participates in protein processing and membrane production.

questions.prompt: This membrane network lacks bound ribosomes and is associated with lipid synthesis, detoxification, and carbohydrate metabolism.
questions.explanation: Smooth ER lacks bound ribosomes and performs these metabolic functions.

sets.title: Golgi directionality
sets.unlock_rule: Schedule only after every associated knowledge record has been encountered in a completed or in-progress story.

questions.prompt: This side of the Golgi receives incoming transport vesicles from the ER.
questions.explanation: The cis face is the receiving side.

questions.prompt: This side sorts and dispatches vesicles toward other destinations.
questions.explanation: The trans face is the shipping side.

sets.title: Digestive versus oxidative organelles
sets.unlock_rule: Schedule only after every associated knowledge record has been encountered in a completed or in-progress story.

questions.prompt: This acidic digestive compartment contains hydrolytic enzymes and participates in breakdown and recycling.
questions.explanation: Lysosomes digest macromolecules and damaged material with hydrolytic enzymes.

questions.prompt: This organelle carries out oxidative reactions and contains enzymes such as catalase that handle hydrogen peroxide.
questions.explanation: Peroxisomes perform oxidative chemistry and manage hydrogen peroxide.

sets.title: Cytoskeletal elements
sets.unlock_rule: Schedule only after every associated knowledge record has been encountered in a completed or in-progress story.

questions.prompt: This hollow cytoskeletal element forms tracks for motor proteins and contributes to the mitotic spindle.
questions.explanation: Microtubules are hollow tubulin structures used in transport and chromosome movement.

questions.prompt: This thin actin-based element supports cell shape changes, contraction, and cell crawling.
questions.explanation: Microfilaments are actin filaments involved in shape and movement.

questions.prompt: This rope-like element provides durable mechanical strength and helps stabilize cell structure.
questions.explanation: Intermediate filaments provide tensile strength and structural stability.

sets.title: Chloroplast internal structures
sets.unlock_rule: Schedule only after every associated knowledge record has been encountered in a completed or in-progress story.

questions.prompt: This is one flattened membrane sac whose membrane contains chlorophyll and supports light-dependent reactions.
questions.explanation: A thylakoid is an individual membrane sac.

questions.prompt: This is a stack of thylakoids.
questions.explanation: A granum is a stack of thylakoid membrane sacs inside a chloroplast.

questions.prompt: This fluid region surrounds thylakoids and contains enzymes used in the Calvin cycle.
questions.explanation: The stroma is the chloroplast fluid outside the thylakoids.

sets.title: Membrane protein placement
sets.unlock_rule: Schedule only after every associated knowledge record has been encountered in a completed or in-progress story.

questions.prompt: This protein penetrates the hydrophobic interior of the bilayer but does not necessarily cross the whole membrane.
questions.explanation: Integral proteins penetrate the bilayer; some are transmembrane and some are not.

questions.prompt: This protein is loosely attached to the membrane surface or to exposed portions of another protein.
questions.explanation: Peripheral proteins remain associated with the membrane surface.

questions.prompt: This integral protein spans the bilayer from one side to the other.
questions.explanation: A transmembrane protein crosses the entire bilayer.

sets.title: Membrane carbohydrate labels
sets.unlock_rule: Schedule only after every associated knowledge record has been encountered in a completed or in-progress story.

questions.prompt: A membrane carbohydrate chain is covalently attached to a lipid.
questions.explanation: A glycolipid is a lipid with an attached carbohydrate.

questions.prompt: A membrane carbohydrate chain is covalently attached to a protein.
questions.explanation: A glycoprotein is a protein with an attached carbohydrate.

sets.title: Transport energy and mechanism
sets.unlock_rule: Schedule only after every associated knowledge record has been encountered in a completed or in-progress story.

questions.prompt: Net movement occurs down a gradient without direct metabolic-energy input.
questions.explanation: Passive transport does not directly require metabolic energy.

questions.prompt: A solute moves down its gradient through a channel or carrier without direct energy input.
questions.explanation: Facilitated diffusion is passive but uses a membrane protein.

questions.prompt: A membrane transport process requires direct energy input and can build or maintain a gradient.
questions.explanation: Active transport uses energy to move substances in ways that can oppose spontaneous movement.

sets.title: Protein-mediated membrane routes
sets.unlock_rule: Schedule only after every associated knowledge record has been encountered in a completed or in-progress story.

questions.prompt: This membrane protein forms a hydrophilic passageway that selected ions or molecules can move through.
questions.explanation: Channel proteins provide hydrophilic pores.

questions.prompt: This membrane protein binds a solute and changes conformation to move it across the membrane.
questions.explanation: Carrier proteins alternate conformations after binding their solute.

questions.prompt: This specialized channel greatly increases the rate of water movement across a membrane.
questions.explanation: Aquaporins are specialized membrane channels that greatly increase water permeability.

sets.title: Bulk transport direction
sets.unlock_rule: Schedule only after every associated knowledge record has been encountered in a completed or in-progress story.

questions.prompt: The plasma membrane bends inward and pinches off to bring material into the cell in a vesicle.
questions.explanation: Endocytosis brings material into the cell.

questions.prompt: An internal vesicle fuses with the plasma membrane and releases material outside the cell.
questions.explanation: Exocytosis releases vesicle contents outside the cell.

sets.title: Endocytosis subtypes
sets.unlock_rule: Schedule only after every associated knowledge record has been encountered in a completed or in-progress story.

questions.prompt: A cell engulfs a large particle or microorganism.
questions.explanation: Phagocytosis is uptake of large particles.

questions.prompt: A cell nonspecifically takes in extracellular fluid and dissolved substances.
questions.explanation: Pinocytosis samples extracellular fluid.

questions.prompt: Specific ligands bind surface receptors and are concentrated before vesicle uptake.
questions.explanation: Receptor-mediated endocytosis selectively concentrates receptor-bound cargo.

sets.title: Tonicity
sets.unlock_rule: Schedule only after every associated knowledge record has been encountered in a completed or in-progress story.

questions.prompt: Relative to the cell, this solution causes net water entry.
questions.explanation: A hypotonic environment drives net water into the cell.

questions.prompt: Relative to the cell, opposing water movements balance so there is no net change in water amount.
questions.explanation: An isotonic environment has no net water movement even though water still moves both ways.

questions.prompt: Relative to the cell, this solution causes net water loss.
questions.explanation: A hypertonic environment drives net water out of the cell.

sets.title: Water-potential components
sets.unlock_rule: Schedule only after every associated knowledge record has been encountered in a completed or in-progress story.

questions.prompt: This total predicts the direction of net water movement and equals the sum of pressure and solute components.
questions.explanation: Water potential combines pressure potential and solute potential: Ψ = Ψp + Ψs.

questions.prompt: This component represents physical pressure and can be positive in a turgid plant cell.
questions.explanation: Pressure potential is the physical-pressure contribution to total water potential.

questions.prompt: This component becomes more negative as dissolved-solute concentration increases.
questions.explanation: Solute potential is zero for pure water under the standard convention and negative for solutions.

sets.title: Electrochemical transport
sets.unlock_rule: Schedule only after every associated knowledge record has been encountered in a completed or in-progress story.

questions.prompt: This general type of pump contributes to membrane voltage because its transport cycle moves net charge across the membrane.
questions.explanation: Electrogenic pumps create net charge separation.

questions.prompt: In animal cells, this ATP-driven pump moves 3 Na⁺ out and 2 K⁺ in per cycle.
questions.explanation: The sodium-potassium pump has a 3 Na⁺ out / 2 K⁺ in stoichiometry per ATP.

questions.prompt: This ATP-driven transporter builds an H⁺ electrochemical gradient across a membrane.
questions.explanation: A proton pump uses energy to move H⁺ and build a gradient.

questions.prompt: This mechanism couples downhill movement of one substance to uphill movement of another.
questions.explanation: Cotransport uses energy stored in an existing gradient.

sets.title: Energy organelles
sets.unlock_rule: Schedule only after every associated knowledge record has been encountered in a completed or in-progress story.

questions.prompt: This double-membrane organelle contains an intermembrane space, a matrix, and an inner membrane folded into cristae.
questions.explanation: Mitochondria contain cristae and a matrix and participate in aerobic cellular respiration.

questions.prompt: This double-membrane organelle contains thylakoids, grana, stroma, and chlorophyll and carries out photosynthesis.
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain thylakoid membranes and stroma and perform photosynthesis.
